figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of CMMs and transition constraints. (a) The observed attribute A influences a modulation variable Λ, which modulates the latent concept C, which generates the observation X. (b,c) Valid concept and mixing transitions are concept-space transformations that can be absorbed into the corresponding model class. Arrows in (b) denote equivalence after restriction to Ao, while arrows in (c) read K ν =K′Tτv ν =K′′Tτb . (d) The transition-intersection criterion selects transitions valid on both sides; if their intersection is contained in G, the CMM is identifiable up to ∼G (Thm. 1).

Table 2: Variable-level CMM translations for representative prior work. Each row records the objects along the chain A → Λ → C → X, following notations in the original papers. In the mechanism-based CRL rows, Gλ denotes the induced DAG from local mechanisms λ.

Table 3: Operator-level CMM translations for representative prior work. Each row records the three kernels in the CMM chain A → Λ → C → X. For Hyvarinen et al. [2019], Γ(λ) is the normalizer determined by the tuple λ = (qi) k i=1, not an additional modulator component. For [Khemakhem et al., 2020a], K̃ denotes a kernel that adds noise, which are injective through deconvolution process. In the Gaussian CRL row, η(i) is the shift parameter used in that model, not an indexing map. In the mechanism-based CRL rows, λ denotes a tuple of local mechanisms and Gλ denotes the DAG induced by those mechanisms. For topic models, Φ ∈ Rr×n denotes the topic-word matrix, so K(V = v | T = t) = Φtv.
